# Mashamba

> Mashamba, FFP (U) Ltd is a Ugandan fresh produce airfreight exporter, supplying 28 export product lines (14 available all year) to wholesale buyers in the UK, the EU and the Gulf, with fast, careful handling from packhouse to aircraft and full export documentation.

Mashamba is the trading name of FFP (U) Ltd, a registered exporter of horticultural products based in Kampala, Uganda. Export operations have run since 2001 through the parent company Icemark-Africa, and the Mashamba brand has traded since 2008. The company sources from a registered grower network, grades and packs produce in vented 4 to 10 kg cartons, and airfreights it from Entebbe, shipping more than 40 tonnes a week at peak. Lines include hot pepper and chilli, ginger, matoke, West Indian avocados, white Lumonde sweet potatoes, white African eggplant (garden egg), cocoyam, sugar cane, apple bananas, pineapples and seasonal Hass avocados. Buyers can review the range, request an export quote, start with a trial shipment of 100 boxes per line, and read free export guides.

- [Get an Export Quote](https://ffpmashamba.com/get-quotes): Build your shipment by product and box code, then send it by email or WhatsApp for a tailored export quote.
- [Contact Us](https://ffpmashamba.com/contact-us): Reach Mashamba's export team by form, phone or WhatsApp.

## Products (crops)

- [Ugandan Hot Peppers](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-hot-peppers): Fresh hot pepper (100,000 to 350,000 SHU) and chilli, from registered grower sites, airfreighted from Entebbe.
- [Ugandan Ginger](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-ginger): Fresh, mature, high-gingerol ginger root, available near year-round.
- [Ugandan Matoke](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-matoke): Fresh green East African Highland cooking banana, shipped green and handled with care at every step.
- [Ugandan Avocados](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-avocados): West Indian jumbo avocados, smooth green skin, 250 to 700 g, available year-round.
- [Ugandan Sweet Potatoes](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-sweet-potatoes): Dry, starchy white-fleshed Lumonde sweet potato, cured and soil-free for export.
- [Ugandan White African Eggplant](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-white-african-eggplant): Fresh white African eggplant (garden egg) for the African-food trade.
- [Ugandan Cocoyam](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-cocoyam): Fresh cocoyam corms, malanga and eddoe, cured and soil-free for the diaspora kitchen.
- [Ugandan Sugar Cane](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-sugar-cane): Fresh-cut Ugandan sugar cane for chewing and juice.
- [Ugandan Apple Bananas](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-apple-bananas): Sweet Sukali Ndizi apple bananas, airfreighted fresh.
- [Ugandan Hass Avocados](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-hass-avocados): Hass avocados in season from about January to September, packed in 4 kg cartons.
- [Ugandan Pineapples](https://ffpmashamba.com/products/ugandan-pineapples): Smooth Cayenne pineapples cut at eating ripeness, available all year and flown crown-on.

## Markets

- [Uganda Fresh Produce to the UK](https://ffpmashamba.com/markets/uganda-fresh-produce-uk): Ugandan produce flown Entebbe to London Gatwick, duty-free under the DCTS and pre-notified through IPAFFS.
- [Uganda Fresh Produce to the UAE](https://ffpmashamba.com/markets/uganda-fresh-produce-uae): Ginger, hot peppers and matoke landed in Dubai at 0% GCC duty within days of harvest.
- [Uganda Fresh Produce to Saudi Arabia](https://ffpmashamba.com/markets/uganda-fresh-produce-saudi-arabia): Ugandan fresh produce supplied to Saudi buyers by air, SFDA-ready.
- [Uganda Fresh Produce to the Netherlands](https://ffpmashamba.com/markets/uganda-fresh-produce-netherlands): Ugandan hot peppers, ginger and matoke for Dutch importers and wholesalers, duty-free under EBA.
- [Uganda Fresh Produce to Germany](https://ffpmashamba.com/markets/uganda-fresh-produce-germany): Matoke, hot pepper and ginger for German importers and Afro-food wholesalers, EU duty-free under EBA.

## Export guides

- [Export Resources Hub](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources): Practical guides to sourcing fresh produce from Uganda, the export process, documentation, destination markets and field reports.
- [Why Source Produce From Uganda](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/why-source-produce-from-uganda): Why UK, EU and Gulf buyers choose Uganda, year-round equatorial supply and distinctive varieties.
- [How to Choose a Ugandan Produce Exporter](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/how-to-choose-ugandan-produce-exporter): The registrations, handling records and references to check before you order.
- [The Airfreight Export Process](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/uganda-airfreight-export-process): Uganda's airfreight export process, step by step from farm to buyer.
- [Export Documentation Guide](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/uganda-export-documentation-guide): The five-document pack that clears Ugandan produce into the UK and EU, including the phytosanitary certificate, IPAFFS and TRACES.
- [Entebbe-London Air Route](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/uganda-airlines-gatwick-route): The direct Entebbe to London Gatwick cargo route explained for produce buyers.
- [Seasonal Availability Calendar](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/uganda-fresh-produce-seasonal-availability): When Ugandan produce is in season, a month-by-month availability guide and why Uganda supplies year-round.
- [Who Buys Ugandan Produce in the UK & Europe](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/who-buys-ugandan-produce-uk-eu): The buyer groups behind UK and EU demand for Ugandan produce, from diaspora retail to wholesale markets.
- [Uganda vs Kenya: Sourcing Compared](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/uganda-vs-kenya-fresh-produce-sourcing): Choosing your East African produce origin, how Uganda and Kenya compare for fresh produce buyers.

## Field reports

- [Fruit Attraction 2026: Four Buyer Meetings in Madrid](https://ffpmashamba.com/resources/fruit-attraction-2026-buyer-meetings): Mashamba's report from Fruit Attraction 2026 (IFEMA MADRID, 6 to 8 October 2026), where its Operations Director joined an ITC-supported group of African exporters and met importers from France, Germany and Spain.
